name: runfile
description: Contributes VS Code tasks generated at runtime by a shell command, so a project's tasks appear in Run Task without ever being written to tasks.json.

task.description: The name of the target to run.

dir.description: Directory `run` starts discovery from (passed as `run --dir`). Omit to discover from the workspace folder.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No Runfile targets were found in this workspace.
[Refresh](command:runfile.refresh)

If you expected targets here, check the [output log](command:runfile.showLog) for a failing generate command.

runfile.catalogCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command run in each workspace folder to list targets as JSON on **stdout** — the `{ "formatVersion": 1, "targets": [...] }` document emitted by `run :list --json`. Discovery is the CLI's job, so it needs no flags: it walks up for the nearest `runfiles/`, down for subproject ones, and folds in the machine-wide `~/.runfiles/`. Anything on stderr is ignored. Re-run every time VS Code fetches tasks — keep it cheap.

runfile.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show an inline **Run** button at the top of every `.run` file inside a `runfiles/` directory. One target is one file, so there is one button per file. It runs `run --stdin-args --dir <the runfiles parent> <target>`, so a target in a subproject runs under the name that directory gives it. `_shared.run` gets no button — it configures a directory rather than being a target.

runfile.enabled.description: Contribute dynamically generated tasks. Turn off to stop running the generate command entirely.

runfile.interactive.markdownDescription: Run tasks that pass `--stdin-args` inside an interactive pseudoterminal so `run` can prompt for missing arguments and read your answers from the terminal. Turn off to run them as plain shell tasks (stdin prompts will fail, matching VS Code's default task behaviour).

runfile.lsp.markdownDescription: Report errors in `.run` files as you type, using the `runfile-lsp` language server. Diagnostics come from the same parser `run` itself uses, so the editor and the runner cannot disagree. Turn off if the server is not installed.

runfile.lspPath.description: Path to the runfile-lsp executable. Looked up on PATH when left as a bare name.
